name: Evo 2 (Arc Institute)
subcategory: genomic (DNA) foundation model across all domains of life
origin_detail: Arc Institute (non-profit research institute); NVIDIA provides NIM hosting, a hosted API and a BioNeMo fine-tuning tutorial; pretrained with the Savanna framework.
openness_notes: Code Apache-2.0 (GitHub); evo2_40b weights Apache-2.0 (Hugging Face); training data OpenGenome2 Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face (8.8 trillion base pairs, 5.52 TB, from GTDB v220, IMG/PR, MGD, IMG/VR, NCBI, Ensembl, EPDnew, RNAcentral, Rfam and organelles). bioRxiv 2025-02-18; Nature 2026 (DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10176-5). A biosafety exclusion of eukaryotic viral genomes is often reported but was not confirmed on fetched pages. Score 4: code, weights and training data all permissively licensed, from a non-profit.
robustness: Everything needed to retrain is public under Apache-2.0; NVIDIA hosting adds a commercial access path but no lock-in.
physical_science_relevance: Biology and biochemistry (genome design and variant-effect prediction); a full-stack open model at frontier scale (40B).

training_data.name: OpenGenome2
training_data.note: 8.8 trillion base pairs across prokaryotes, eukaryotes, metagenomes, viruses (IMG/VR), RNA and organelles.

openness_effect_assessment: Releasing the training data along with the weights made Evo 2 reproducible, and the dataset is downloaded more than the flagship model (12k vs 8k a month). Corporate partners (NVIDIA) monetise hosting rather than the model.
key_takeaway: The fullest release in the group: a non-profit published a 40B frontier-scale model with its training data under Apache-2.0. Non-profit, philanthropically funded labs are the most reliable source of fully open AI for science.
